replies.author: @Nate2.4
replies.text: ​@ਮਨਪ੍ਰੀਤ-ਪ1ਚWhat do u mean. It is accessible first to the Vietnames masses. The script became a beacon of anti-imperalism and their nationalist leaders opted it to mass educate the people at fast pace so that they could understand and decipher the propaganda of the colonial powers at that time. It served greater purpose for Vietnamese people and not the other way around. The chinese blended scripts which formally Vietnamese scholars adapted was too complicated to learn and was just in vogue for the upper class and people with power. There was no way to educate the masses in little time when their society was transforming at high pace. And so they adopted the already popular easy Latin script. Their indeginous Chibese blended scripts never was popular among them in the 1st place. Different situations and different purpose led to the very emergence of modern Vietnamese Latin script which was meticulously constructed to justify every Vietnamese sounds by the missionaries when translating their religious texts much better than their former difficult script could.

replies.author: @huyduong5486
replies.text: @ਮਨਪ੍ਰੀਤ-ਪ1ਚ actually there was 2 attempts (afaik) to create a new script for Vietnamese language based on Chinese character, Chữ Nôm is the first one, created during the First Era of Northern Domination to resist against Han Chinese assimilation, but it was insanely hard, you have to learn to read and write Chinese before you can ever understand Chữ Nôm. Besides it was never standardized and people had to guess what the word means. The second one is Quốc Âm Tân Tự, which is a syllabary making it easier to learn but never got the push to replace the old combination of Chữ Nôm and Chữ Hán. After a while the French came and adopt the Latin alphabet to simplify the language since it was more familiar to them.
